label: Printer absolute correction
tooltip: Will inflate or deflate the sliced 2D polygons according to the sign of the correction.

label: Pressure advance
tooltip: Pressure advance(Klipper) AKA Linear advance factor(Marlin)

label: Arc fitting
tooltip: Enable to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. G-code resolution will be used as the fitting tolerance.

label: Area fill threshold
tooltip: The value is expressed as a percentage of the bed area. If the area of a particular layer is smaller than 'area_fill', then 'Below area fill threshold' parameters are used to determine the layer separation (tearing) procedure. Otherwise 'Above area fill threshold' parameters are used.

label: Emit temperature commands automatically
tooltip:
When enabled, QIDISlicer will check whether your custom Start G-Code contains G-codes to set extruder, bed or chamber temperature (M104, M109, M140, M190, M141 and M191). If so, the temperatures will not be emitted automatically so you're free to customize the order of heating commands and other custom actions. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all QIDISlicer settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want.
If your custom Start G-Code does NOT contain these G-codes, QIDISlicer will execute the Start G-Code after heated chamber was set to its temperature, bed reached its target temperature and extruder just started heating.

When disabled, QIDISlicer will NOT emit commands to heat up extruder, bed or chamber, leaving all to Custom Start G-Code.

label: Automatic extrusion widths calculation
tooltip: Automatically calculates extrusion widths based on the nozzle diameter of the currently used extruder. This setting is essential for printing with different nozzle diameters.

label: Automatic infill combination
tooltip: This feature automatically combines infill of several layers and speeds up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus maintaining accuracy.

label: Automatic infill combination - Max layer height
tooltip: Maximum layer height for combining infill when automatic infill combining is enabled. Maximum layer height could be specified either as an absolute in millimeters value or as a percentage of nozzle diameter. For printing with different nozzle diameters, it is recommended to use percentage value over absolute value.

label: Auxiliary Fan
tooltip: Enable rapid cooling fan control.

label: Avoid crossing curled overhangs (Experimental)
tooltip: Plan travel moves such that the extruder avoids areas where the filament may be curled up. This is mostly happening on steeper rounded overhangs and may cause a crash with the nozzle. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

label: Avoid crossing perimeters
tooltip: Optimize travel moves in order to minimize the crossing of perimeters. This is mostly useful with Bowden extruders which suffer from oozing. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

label: Avoid crossing perimeters - Max detour length
tooltip: The maximum detour length for avoid crossing perimeters. If the detour is longer than this value, avoid crossing perimeters is not applied for this travel path. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path.

label: Other layers
tooltip: Bed temperature for layers after the first one. Set this to zero to disable bed temperature control commands in the output.

label: Bed temperature by extruder
tooltip: The extruder which determines bed temperatures. Set to 0 to determine temperatures based on the first printing extruder of the first and the second layers.

label: Before layer change G-code
tooltip: This custom code is inserted at every layer change, right before the Z move. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings as well as [layer_num] and [layer_z].

label: Between objects G-code
tooltip: This code is inserted between objects when using sequential printing. By default extruder and bed temperature are reset using non-wait command; however if M104, M109, M140 or M190 are detected in this custom code, Slic3r will not add temperature commands. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want.

label: Supports binary G-code
tooltip: Enable, if the firmware supports binary G-code format (bgcode). To generate .bgcode files, make sure you have binary G-code enabled in Configuration->Preferences->Other.

label: Cost
tooltip: Cost

label: Bottle volume
tooltip: Bottle volume

label: Bottle weight
tooltip: Bottle weight

label: Bottom fill pattern
tooltip: Fill pattern for bottom infill. This only affects the bottom external visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

label: Bottom surface flow ratio
tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill

label: Bottom
tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on bottom surfaces.

label: Bottom
tooltip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased above bottom_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of bottom shell.

label: Box id
tooltip: ID of the printer.

label: BOX temperature
tooltip: BOX temperature.

label: BOX Temperature
tooltip: Enable box temperature control.

label: Support base diameter
tooltip: Diameter in mm of the pillar base

label: Support base height
tooltip: The height of the pillar base cone

label: Support base safety distance
tooltip: The minimum distance of the pillar base from the model in mm. Makes sense in zero elevation mode where a gap according to this parameter is inserted between the model and the pad.

label: Support on build plate only
tooltip: Only create support if it lies on a build plate. Don't create support on a print.

label: Critical angle
tooltip: The default angle for connecting support sticks and junctions.

label: Pinhead front diameter
tooltip: Diameter of the pointing side of the head

label: Head penetration
tooltip: How much the pinhead has to penetrate the model surface

label: Pinhead width
tooltip: Width from the back sphere center to the front sphere center

label: Max bridge length
tooltip: The max length of a bridge

label: Max bridges on a pillar
tooltip: Maximum number of bridges that can be placed on a pillar. Bridges hold support point pinheads and connect to pillars as small branches.

label: Max pillar linking distance
tooltip: The max distance of two pillars to get linked with each other. A zero value will prohibit pillar cascading.

label: Max weight on model
tooltip: Maximum weight of sub-trees that terminate on the model instead of the print bed. The weight is the sum of the lenghts of all branches emanating from the endpoint.

label: Object elevation
tooltip: How much the supports should lift up the supported object. If "Pad around object" is enabled, this value is ignored.

label: Pillar connection mode
tooltip: Controls the bridge type between two neighboring pillars. Can be zig-zag, cross (double zig-zag) or dynamic which will automatically switch between the first two depending on the distance of the two pillars.

label: Pillar diameter
tooltip: Diameter in mm of the support pillars

label: Pillar widening factor
tooltip: Merging bridges or pillars into another pillars can increase the radius. Zero means no increase, one means full increase. The exact amount of increase is unspecified and can change in the future.

label: Small pillar diameter percent
tooltip: The percentage of smaller pillars compared to the normal pillar diameter which are used in problematic areas where a normal pilla cannot fit.

label: Bridge
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for bridges. Set zero to disable acceleration control for bridges.

label: Bridging angle
tooltip: Bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for all bridges. Use 180° for zero angle.

label: Bridges fan speed
tooltip: This fan speed is enforced during all bridges and overhangs.

label: Bridge flow ratio
tooltip: This factor affects the amount of plastic for bridging. You can decrease it slightly to pull the extrudates and prevent sagging, although default settings are usually good and you should experiment with cooling (use a fan) before tweaking this.

label: Bridges
tooltip: Speed for printing bridges.

label: Brim separation gap
tooltip: Offset of brim from the printed object. The offset is applied after the elephant foot compensation.

label: Brim type
tooltip: The places where the brim will be printed around each object on the first layer.

label: Brim width
tooltip: The horizontal width of the brim that will be printed around each object on the first layer. When raft is used, no brim is generated (use raft_first_layer_expansion).

label: Chamber Fan
tooltip: Enable chamber fan control.

label: Minimal
tooltip:
Minimal chamber temperature that the printer waits for before the print starts. This allows to start the print before the nominal chamber temperature is reached.
When set to zero, the minimal chamber temperature is not set in the G-code.

label: Nominal
tooltip:
Required chamber temperature for the print.
When set to zero, the nominal chamber temperature is not set in the G-code.

label: Chamber Temperature
tooltip: Enable chamber temperature control.

label: Color change G-code
tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the color change

label: Colorprint height
tooltip: Heights at which a filament change is to occur.

label: Compatible printers condition
tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.

label: Compatible print profiles condition
tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active print profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active print profile.

label: Complete individual objects
tooltip: When printing multiple objects or copies, this feature will complete each object before moving onto next one (and starting it from its bottom layer). This feature is useful to avoid the risk of ruined prints. Slic3r should warn and prevent you from extruder collisions, but beware.

label: Enable auto cooling
tooltip: This flag enables the automatic cooling logic that adjusts print speed and fan speed according to layer printing time.

label: Cooling tube length
tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

label: Cooling tube position
tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

label: Default
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will be reset to after the role-specific acceleration values are used (perimeter/infill). Set zero to prevent resetting acceleration at all.

label: Default filament profile
tooltip: Default filament profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this filament profile will be activated.

label: Default print profile
tooltip: Default print profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this print profile will be activated.

label: Default SLA material profile
tooltip: Default print profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this print profile will be activated.

label: Default SLA material profile
tooltip: Default print profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this print profile will be activated.

label: Delay after exposure
tooltip: Delay after exposure before layer separation.

label: Delay before exposure
tooltip: Delay before exposure after previous layer separation.

label: Deretraction Speed
tooltip: The speed for loading of a filament into extruder after retraction (it only applies to the extruder motor). If left to zero, the retraction speed is used.

label: Detect narrow internal solid infill
tooltip: This option will auto detect narrow internal solid infill area. If enabled, concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed printing up. Otherwise, rectilinear pattern is used defaultly.

label: Disable fan for the first
tooltip: You can set this to a positive value to disable fan at all during the first layers, so that it does not make adhesion worse.

label: Disable rapid cooling fan for the first
tooltip: You can set this to a positive value to disable rapid cooling fan at all during the first layers, so that it does not make adhesion worse.

label: Display height
tooltip: Height of the display

label: Mirror horizontally
tooltip: Enable horizontal mirroring of output images

label: Mirror vertically
tooltip: Enable vertical mirroring of output images

label: Display orientation
tooltip: Set the actual LCD display orientation inside the SLA printer. Portrait mode will flip the meaning of display width and height parameters and the output images will be rotated by 90 degrees.

label: X
tooltip: Number of pixels in X

label: Y
tooltip: Number of pixels in Y

label: Display width
tooltip: Width of the display

label: Don't slow down outer walls
tooltip:
If enabled, this setting will ensure external perimeters are not slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. This is particularly helpful in the below scenarios:

 1. To avoid changes in shine when printing glossy filaments 
2. To avoid changes in external wall speed which may create slight wall artefacts that appear like z banding 
3. To avoid printing at speeds which cause VFAs (fine artefacts) on the external walls

label: Don't support bridges
tooltip: Experimental option for preventing support material from being generated under bridged areas.

label: Draft shield
tooltip:
With draft shield active, the skirt will be printed skirt_distance from the object, possibly intersecting brim.
Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object.
Limited = skirt is as tall as specified by skirt_height.
This is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft.

label: Distance between copies
tooltip: Distance used for the auto-arrange feature of the plater.

label: Elephant foot compensation
tooltip: The first layer will be shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value to compensate for the 1st layer squish aka an Elephant Foot effect.

label: Elephant foot compensation layers
tooltip: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.

label: Elephant foot minimum width
tooltip: Minimum width of features to maintain when doing elephant foot compensation.

label: Enable pressure advance
tooltip: Enable pressure advance, auto calibration result will be overwriten once enabled.

label: Seal
tooltip: This setting represents the PWM your rapid cooling fan needs to work when the printing is sealing.

label: Unseal
tooltip: This setting represents the PWM your rapid cooling fan needs to work when the printing is unsealing.

label: Enable dynamic fan speeds
tooltip: This setting enables dynamic fan speed control on overhangs.

label: Enable dynamic overhang speeds
tooltip: This setting enables dynamic speed control on overhangs.

label: Chamber Fan Speed
tooltip: This setting represents the PWM your volume fan needs to work.

label: End G-code
tooltip: This end procedure is inserted at the end of the output file, before the printer end gcode (and before any toolchange from this filament in case of multimaterial printers). Note that you can use placeholder variables for all QIDISlicer settings. If you have multiple extruders, the gcode is processed in extruder order.
default: "; Filament-specific end gcode \n;END gcode for filament\n"

label: End G-code
tooltip: This end procedure is inserted at the end of the output file. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all QIDISlicer settings.
default:
M104 S0 ; turn off temperature
G28 X0  ; home X axis
M84     ; disable motors

label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
tooltip: Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers).

label: Exposure time
tooltip: Exposure time

label: External perimeters
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for external perimeters. Set zero to use the value for perimeters.

label: External perimeters
tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for external perimeters. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%), it will be computed over layer height.

label: External perimeters
tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of external perimeters (the visible ones). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

label: External perimeters first
tooltip: Print contour perimeters from the outermost one to the innermost one instead of the default inverse order.

label: Extra loading distance
tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further,  if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

label: Extra perimeters if needed
tooltip: Add more perimeters when needed for avoiding gaps in sloping walls. Slic3r keeps adding perimeters, until more than 70% of the loop immediately above is supported.

label: Extra perimeters on overhangs (Experimental)
tooltip: Detect overhang areas where bridges cannot be anchored, and fill them with extra perimeter paths. These paths are anchored to the nearby non-overhang area when possible.

label: Extruder
tooltip: The extruder to use (unless more specific extruder settings are specified). This value overrides perimeter and infill extruders, but not the support extruders.

label: Height
tooltip:
Only used when 'Print Settings -> Complete individual objects' is active. Set this to the vertical distance between your nozzle tip and (usually) the X carriage rods. Used to check for collisions with previously printed objects and to prevent them when arranging.
The value is ignored for most QIDI printers, which come with more detailed extruder model.

label: Radius
tooltip:
Only used when 'Print Settings -> Complete individual objects' is active. Set this to a radius of a nozzle-centered cylinder big enough to enclose the extruder assembly. Used to check for collisions with previously printed objects and to prevent them when arranging.
The value is ignored for most QIDI printers, which come with more detailed extruder model.

label: Extruder Color
tooltip: This is only used in the Slic3r interface as a visual help.

label: Extruder offset
tooltip: If your firmware doesn't handle the extruder displacement you need the G-code to take it into account. This option lets you specify the displacement of each extruder with respect to the first one. It expects positive coordinates (they will be subtracted from the XY coordinate).

label: Extrusion axis
tooltip: Use this option to set the axis letter associated to your printer's extruder (usually E but some printers use A).

label: Extrusion multiplier
tooltip: This factor changes the amount of flow proportionally. You may need to tweak this setting to get nice surface finish and correct single wall widths. Usual values are between 0.9 and 1.1. If you think you need to change this more, check filament diameter and your firmware E steps.

label: Default extrusion width
tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to allow a manual extrusion width. If left to zero, Slic3r derives extrusion widths from the nozzle diameter (see the tooltips for perimeter extrusion width, infill extrusion width etc). If expressed as percentage (for example: 230%), it will be computed over layer height.

label: Faded layers
tooltip: Number of the layers needed for the exposure time fade from initial exposure time to the exposure time

label: Keep fan always on
tooltip: If this is enabled, fan will never be disabled and will be kept running at least at its minimum speed. Useful for PLA, harmful for ABS.

label: Enable fan if layer print time is below
tooltip: If layer print time is estimated below this number of seconds, fan will be enabled and its speed will be calculated by interpolating the minimum and maximum speeds.

label: Fast
tooltip: Time of the fast tilt

label: Abrasive material
tooltip: This flag means that the material is abrasive and requires a hardened nozzle. The value is used by the printer to check it.

label: Color
tooltip: This is only used in the Slic3r interface as a visual help.

label: Speed of the last cooling move
tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating towards this speed.

label: Speed of the first cooling move
tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating beginning at this speed.

label: Number of cooling moves
tooltip: Filament is cooled by being moved back and forth in the cooling tubes. Specify desired number of these moves.

label: Cost
tooltip: Enter your filament cost per kg here. This is only for statistical information.

label: Density
tooltip: Enter your filament density here. This is only for statistical information. A decent way is to weigh a known length of filament and compute the ratio of the length to volume. Better is to calculate the volume directly through displacement.

label: Deretraction Speed
tooltip: The speed for loading of a filament into extruder after retraction (it only applies to the extruder motor). If left to zero, the retraction speed is used.

label: Diameter
tooltip: Enter your filament diameter here. Good precision is required, so use a caliper and do multiple measurements along the filament, then compute the average.

label: Flush
tooltip: Nozzle temperature for the Filament flush.

label: Max crossing infill speed
tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill with self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

label: Max non-crossing infill speed
tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill without any self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

label: Filament load time
tooltip: Time for the printer firmware (or the Multi Material Unit 2.0) to load a new filament during a tool change (when executing the T code). This time is added to the total print time by the G-code time estimator.

label: Loading speed
tooltip: Speed used for loading the filament on the wipe tower.

label: Loading speed at the start
tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

label: Max volumetric speed
tooltip: Maximum volumetric speed allowed for this filament. Limits the maximum volumetric speed of a print to the minimum of print and filament volumetric speed. Set to zero for no limit.

label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, Slic3r will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

label: Enable ramming for multitool setups
tooltip: Perform ramming when using multitool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the toolchange. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

label: Multitool ramming flow
tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the toolchange.

label: Multitool ramming volume
tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the toolchange.

label: Filament notes
tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

label: Purge volume multiplier
tooltip: Purging volume on the wipe tower is determined by 'multimaterial_purging' in Printer Settings. This option allows to modify the volume on filament level. Note that the project can override this by setting project-specific values.

label: Ramming parameters
tooltip: This string is edited by RammingDialog and contains ramming specific parameters.

label: Minimum travel after retraction
tooltip: Retraction is not triggered when travel moves are shorter than this length.

label: Retract amount before wipe
tooltip: With bowden extruders, it may be wise to do some amount of quick retract before doing the wipe movement.

label: Retract on layer change
tooltip: This flag enforces a retraction whenever a Z move is done.

label: Retraction length
tooltip: When retraction is triggered, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

label: Length
tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

label: Lift height
tooltip: Lift height applied before travel.

label: Above Z
tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for skipping lift on the first layers.

label: Below Z
tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for limiting lift to the first layers.

label: Deretraction extra length
tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

label: Extra length on restart
tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

label: Retraction Speed
tooltip: The speed for retractions (it only applies to the extruder motor).

label: Seam gap distance
tooltip: The distance between the endpoints of a closed loop perimeter. Positive values will shorten and interrupt the loop slightly to reduce the seam. Negative values will extend the loop, causing the endpoints to overlap slightly. When percents are used, the distance is derived from the nozzle diameter. Set to zero to disable this feature.

label: Shrinkage compensation XY
tooltip: Enter your filament shrinkage percentages for the X and Y axes here to apply scaling of the object to compensate for shrinkage in the X and Y axes. For example, if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%.

label: Shrinkage compensation Z
tooltip: Enter your filament shrinkage percentages for the Z axis here to apply scaling of the object to compensate for shrinkage in the Z axis. For example, if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%.

label: Soluble material
tooltip: Soluble material is most likely used for a soluble support.

label: Spool weight
tooltip: Enter weight of the empty filament spool. One may weigh a partially consumed filament spool before printing and one may compare the measured weight with the calculated weight of the filament with the spool to find out whether the amount of filament on the spool is sufficient to finish the print.

label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
tooltip: If set to nonzero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

label: Stamping loading speed
tooltip: Speed used for stamping.

label: Delay after unloading
tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable toolchanges with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
tooltip: If enabled, QIDISlicer detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

label: Maximum ramping lift
tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

label: Use ramping lift
tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

label: Ramping slope angle
tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

label: Filament type
tooltip: The filament material type for use in custom G-codes.

label: Filament unload time
tooltip: Time for the printer firmware (or the Multi Material Unit 2.0) to unload a filament during a tool change (when executing the T code). This time is added to the total print time by the G-code time estimator.

label: Unloading speed
tooltip: Speed used for unloading the filament on the wipe tower (does not affect  initial part of unloading just after ramming).

label: Unloading speed at the start
tooltip: Speed used for unloading the tip of the filament immediately after ramming.

label: Wipe while retracting
tooltip: This flag will move the nozzle while retracting to minimize the possible blob on leaky extruders.

label: Wipe Distance
tooltip: Discribe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

label: Fill angle
tooltip: Default base angle for infill orientation. Cross-hatching will be applied to this. Bridges will be infilled using the best direction Slic3r can detect, so this setting does not affect them.

label: Fill density
tooltip: Density of internal infill, expressed in the range 0% - 100%.

label: Fill pattern
tooltip: Fill pattern for general low-density infill.

label: Filter out tiny top gaps infill
tooltip: Filter out gaps smaller than the threshold specified. This setting affact top surface's gap infill

label: First layer
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer.

label: First object layer over raft interface
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer of object above raft interface. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer of object above raft interface.

label: First layer
tooltip: Heated build plate temperature for the first layer. Set this to zero to disable bed temperature control commands in the output.

label: First layer
tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for first layer. You can use this to force fatter extrudates for better adhesion. If expressed as percentage (for example 120%) it will be computed over first layer height. If set to zero, it will use the default extrusion width.

label: First layer height
tooltip: When printing with very low layer heights, you might still want to print a thicker bottom layer to improve adhesion and tolerance for non perfect build plates.

label: First layer solid infill speed
tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the solid infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the solid infill speed (for example: 40% of the solid infill speed). Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

label: First layer speed
tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first layer, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

label: Speed of object first layer over raft interface
tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first object layer above raft interface, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

label: First layer
tooltip: Nozzle temperature for the first layer. If you want to control temperature manually during print, set this to zero to disable temperature control commands in the output G-code.

label: First layer travel
tooltip: Speed for travel moves of the first layer (jumps between distant extrusion points).

label: Full fan speed at layer
tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "disable_fan_first_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "disable_fan_first_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "disable_fan_first_layers" + 1.

label: Fuzzy Skin
tooltip: Fuzzy skin type.

label: Fuzzy skin point distance
tooltip: Perimeters will be split into multiple segments by inserting Fuzzy skin points. Lowering the Fuzzy skin point distance will increase the number of randomly offset points on the perimeter wall.

label: Fuzzy skin thickness
tooltip: The maximum distance that each skin point can be offset (both ways), measured perpendicular to the perimeter wall.

label: Printer gamma correction
tooltip: This will apply a gamma correction to the rasterized 2D polygons. A gamma value of zero means thresholding with the threshold in the middle. This behaviour eliminates antialiasing without losing holes in polygons.

label: Fill gaps
tooltip: Enables filling of gaps between perimeters and between the inner most perimeters and infill.

label: Gap fill
tooltip: Speed for filling small gaps using short zigzag moves. Keep this reasonably low to avoid too much shaking and resonance issues. Set zero to disable gaps filling.

label: Verbose G-code
tooltip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

label: G-code flavor
tooltip: Some G/M-code commands, including temperature control and others, are not universal. Set this option to your printer's firmware to get a compatible output. The "No extrusion" flavor prevents QIDISlicer from exporting any extrusion value at all.

label: Label objects
tooltip:
Selects whether labels should be exported at object boundaries and in what format.
OctoPrint = comments to be consumed by OctoPrint CancelObject plugin.
Firmware = firmware specific G-code (it will be chosen based on firmware flavor and it can end up to be empty).

This settings is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

label: G-code resolution
tooltip: Maximum deviation of exported G-code paths from their full resolution counterparts. Very high resolution G-code requires huge amount of RAM to slice and preview, also a 3D printer may stutter not being able to process a high resolution G-code in a timely manner. On the other hand, a low resolution G-code will produce a low poly effect and because the G-code reduction is performed at each layer independently, visible artifacts may be produced.

label: G-code substitutions
tooltip: Find / replace patterns in G-code lines and substitute them.

label: High extruder current on filament swap

tooltip: Defines the pad cavity depth. Set to zero to disable the cavity. Be careful when enabling this feature, as some resins may produce an extreme suction effect inside the cavity, which makes peeling the print off the vat foil difficult.

tooltip: Diameter of the pointing side of the head

label: Head penetration
tooltip: How much the pinhead has to penetrate the model surface

label: Pinhead width
tooltip: Width from the back sphere center to the front sphere center

label: Generate support material
tooltip: Enable support material generation.

label: Pattern angle
tooltip: Use this setting to rotate the support material pattern on the horizontal plane.

label: Auto generated supports
tooltip: If checked, supports will be generated automatically based on the overhang threshold value. If unchecked, supports will be generated inside the "Support Enforcer" volumes only.

label: Bottom contact Z distance
tooltip: The vertical distance between the object top surface and the support material interface. If set to zero, support_material_contact_distance will be used for both top and bottom contact Z distances.

label: Bottom interface layers
tooltip: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material. Set to -1 to use support_material_interface_layers

label: Support on build plate only
tooltip: Only create support if it lies on a build plate. Don't create support on a print.

label: Closing radius
tooltip: For snug supports, the support regions will be merged using morphological closing operation. Gaps smaller than the closing radius will be filled in.

label: Top contact Z distance
tooltip: The vertical distance between object and support material interface. Setting this to 0 will also prevent Slic3r from using bridge flow and speed for the first object layer.

label: Enforce support for the first
full_label: Enforce support for the first n layers
tooltip: Generate support material for the specified number of layers counting from bottom, regardless of whether normal support material is enabled or not and regardless of any angle threshold. This is useful for getting more adhesion of objects having a very thin or poor footprint on the build plate.

label: Support material/raft/skirt extruder
tooltip: The extruder to use when printing support material, raft and skirt (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes).

label: Support material
tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for support material. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over layer height.

label: Interface loops
tooltip: Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.

label: Support material/raft interface extruder
tooltip: The extruder to use when printing support material interface (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes). This affects raft too.

label: Top interface layers
tooltip: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material.

label: Interface pattern
tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.

label: Interface pattern spacing
tooltip: Spacing between interface lines. Set zero to get a solid interface.

label: Support material interface
tooltip: Speed for printing support material interface layers. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%) it will be calculated over support material speed.

label: Pattern
tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material.

label: Pattern spacing
tooltip: Spacing between support material lines.

label: Support material
tooltip: Speed for printing support material.

label: Style
tooltip: Style and shape of the support towers. Projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports, while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.

label: Synchronize with object layers
tooltip: Synchronize support layers with the object print layers. This is useful with multi-material printers, where the extruder switch is expensive. This option is only available when top contact Z distance is set to zero.

label: Overhang threshold
tooltip: Support material will not be generated for overhangs whose slope angle (90° = vertical) is above the given threshold. In other words, this value represent the most horizontal slope (measured from the horizontal plane) that you can print without support material. Set to zero for automatic detection (recommended).

label: With sheath around the support
tooltip: Add a sheath (a single perimeter line) around the base support. This makes the support more reliable, but also more difficult to remove.

label: XY separation between an object and its support
tooltip: XY separation between an object and its support. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%), it will be calculated over external perimeter width.

label: Max bridge length
tooltip: The max length of a bridge

label: Max bridges on a pillar
tooltip: Maximum number of bridges that can be placed on a pillar. Bridges hold support point pinheads and connect to pillars as small branches.

label: Max pillar linking distance
tooltip: The max distance of two pillars to get linked with each other. A zero value will prohibit pillar cascading.

label: Max weight on model
tooltip: Maximum weight of sub-trees that terminate on the model instead of the print bed. The weight is the sum of the lenghts of all branches emanating from the endpoint.

label: Object elevation
tooltip: How much the supports should lift up the supported object. If "Pad around object" is enabled, this value is ignored.

label: Pillar connection mode
tooltip: Controls the bridge type between two neighboring pillars. Can be zig-zag, cross (double zig-zag) or dynamic which will automatically switch between the first two depending on the distance of the two pillars.

label: Pillar diameter
tooltip: Diameter in mm of the support pillars

label: Pillar widening factor
tooltip: Merging bridges or pillars into another pillars can increase the radius. Zero means no increase, one means full increase. The exact amount of increase is unspecified and can change in the future.

label: Support points density
tooltip: This is a relative measure of support points density.

label: Small pillar diameter percent
tooltip: The percentage of smaller pillars compared to the normal pillar diameter which are used in problematic areas where a normal pilla cannot fit.

label: Maximum Branch Angle
tooltip: The maximum angle of the branches, when the branches have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle to be able to have more reach.

label: Preferred Branch Angle
tooltip: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

label: Branch Diameter
tooltip: The diameter of the thinnest branches of organic support. Thicker branches are more sturdy. Branches towards the base will be thicker than this.

label: Branch Diameter Angle
tooltip: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

label: Branch Diameter with double walls
tooltip: Branches with area larger than the area of a circle of this diameter will be printed with double walls for stability. Set this value to zero for no double walls.

label: Branch Distance
tooltip: How far apart the branches need to be when they touch the model. Making this distance small will cause the tree support to touch the model at more points, causing better overhang but making support harder to remove.

label: Tip Diameter
tooltip: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

label: Branch Density
tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

label: Support tree type
tooltip: Support tree building strategy

label: Generate supports
tooltip: Generate supports for the models

label: Other layers
tooltip: Nozzle temperature for layers after the first one. Set this to zero to disable temperature control commands in the output G-code.

label: Custom G-code
tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code

label: Thick bridges
tooltip: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

label: Detect thin walls
tooltip: Detect single-width walls (parts where two extrusions don't fit and we need to collapse them into a single trace).

label: G-code thumbnails
tooltip:
Picture sizes to be stored into a .gcode / .bgcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY/EXT, XxY/EXT, ..."
Currently supported extensions are PNG, QOI and JPG.

label: Format of G-code thumbnails
tooltip: Format of G-code thumbnails: PNG for best quality, JPG for smallest size, QOI for low memory firmware

label: Tilt down cycles
tooltip: Number of cycles to split the rest of the tilt down move.

label: Tilt down delay
tooltip: The delay between tilt-down cycles.

label: Tilt down finish speed
tooltip: Tilt speed used for the rest of the tilt down move.

label: Tilt down initial speed
tooltip: Tilt speed used for an initial portion of tilt down move.

label: Tilt down offset delay
tooltip: Delay after the tilt reaches 'tilt_down_offset_steps' position.

label: Tilt down offset steps
tooltip: Number of steps to move down from the calibrated (horizontal) position with 'tilt_down_initial_speed'.

label: Tilt up cycles
tooltip: Number of cycles to split the rest of the tilt-up.

label: Tilt up delay
tooltip: The delay between tilt-up cycles.

label: Tilt up finish speed
tooltip: Tilt speed used for the rest of the tilt-up.

label: Tilt up initial speed
tooltip: Tilt speed used for an initial portion of tilt up move.

label: Tilt up offset delay
tooltip: Delay after the tilt reaches 'tilt_up_offset_steps' position.

label: Tilt up offset steps
tooltip: Move tilt up to calibrated (horizontal) position minus this offset.

label: Tool change G-code
tooltip: This custom code is inserted before every toolchange. Placeholder variables for all QIDISlicer settings as well as {toolchange_z}, {previous_extruder} and {next_extruder} can be used. When a tool-changing command which changes to the correct extruder is included (such as T{next_extruder}), QIDISlicer will emit no other such command. It is therefore possible to script custom behaviour both before and after the toolchange.

label: Top fill pattern
tooltip: Fill pattern for top infill. This only affects the top visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

label: Top solid infill
tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for top surfaces. You may want to use thinner extrudates to fill all narrow regions and get a smoother finish. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over layer height.

label: Single perimeter on top surfaces
tooltip: Use only one perimeter on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern. Could be applied on topmost surface or all top surfaces.

label: Top solid infill
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for top solid infill. Set zero to use the value for solid infill.

label: Top surface flow ratio
tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish

label: Top solid infill
tooltip: Speed for printing top solid layers (it only applies to the uppermost external layers and not to their internal solid layers). You may want to slow down this to get a nicer surface finish. This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the solid infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

label: Top
tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on top surfaces.

label: Top
tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased above top_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of top shell. This is useful to prevent pillowing effect when printing with variable layer height.

label: Tower hop height
tooltip: The height of the tower raise.

label: Tower speed
tooltip: Tower speed used for tower raise.

label: Travel
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for travel moves. Set zero to disable acceleration control for travel.

label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
tooltip: If enabled, QIDISlicer detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

label: Maximum ramping lift
tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

label: Use ramping lift
tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

label: Ramping slope angle
tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

label: Travel
tooltip: Speed for travel moves (jumps between distant extrusion points).

label: Z travel
tooltip:
Speed for movements along the Z axis.
When set to zero, the value is ignored and regular travel speed is used instead.

label: Use firmware retraction
tooltip: This setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. Note that this has to be supported by firmware.

label: Use relative E distances
tooltip: If your firmware requires relative E values, check this, otherwise leave it unchecked. Most firmwares use absolute values.

label: Use tilt
tooltip: If enabled, tilt is used for layer separation. Otherwise, all the parameters below are ignored.

label: Use volumetric E
tooltip: This experimental setting uses outputs the E values in cubic millimeters instead of linear millimeters. If your firmware doesn't already know filament diameter(s), you can put commands like 'M200 D[filament_diameter_0] T0' in your start G-code in order to turn volumetric mode on and use the filament diameter associated to the filament selected in Slic3r. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

label: Enable variable layer height feature
tooltip: Some printers or printer setups may have difficulties printing with a variable layer height. Enabled by default.

label: Perimeter distribution count
tooltip: The number of perimeters, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer perimeters don't change in width.

label: Perimeter transitioning threshold angle
tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of perimeters. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no perimeters will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center perimeters, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

label: Perimeter transitioning filter margin
tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra perimeter and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum perimeter width - margin, 2 * Minimum perimeter width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

label: Perimeter transition length
tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of perimeters as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the perimeter segments. If expressed as a percentage (for example 100%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

label: Wipe while retracting
tooltip: This flag will move the nozzle while retracting to minimize the possible blob on leaky extruders.

label: Wipe Device
tooltip: Enable wipe device.

label: Wipe Distance
tooltip: Discribe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

label: Wipe into this object's infill
tooltip: Purging after toolchange will be done inside this object's infills. This lowers the amount of waste but may result in longer print time  due to additional travel moves.

label: Wipe into this object
tooltip: Object will be used to purge the nozzle after a toolchange to save material that would otherwise end up in the wipe tower and decrease print time. Colours of the objects will be mixed as a result.

label: Enable
tooltip: Multi material printers may need to prime or purge extruders on tool changes. Extrude the excess material into the wipe tower.

label: Wipe tower
tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for wipe tower. Set zero to disable acceleration control for the wipe tower.

label: Maximal bridging distance
tooltip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

label: Wipe tower brim width
tooltip: Wipe tower brim width

label: Stabilization cone apex angle
tooltip: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

label: Extra flow for purging
tooltip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
tooltip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

label: Wipe tower extruder
tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

label: No sparse layers (EXPERIMENTAL)
tooltip: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no toolchanges. On layers with a toolchange, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

label: Width
tooltip: Width of a wipe tower

label: Purging volumes - matrix
tooltip: This matrix describes volumes (in cubic milimetres) required to purge the new filament on the wipe tower for any given pair of tools.

label: X-Y contour compensation
tooltip: Contour of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes contour bigger. Negative value makes contour smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

label: X-Y hole compensation
tooltip: Holes of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes holes bigger. Negative value makes holes smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

label: XY Size Compensation
tooltip: The object will be grown/shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value (negative = inwards, positive = outwards). This might be useful for fine-tuning hole sizes.

label: Z offset
tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

label: Z compensation
tooltip: Number of layers to Z correct to avoid cross layer bleed
